findings.title: Failure threshold can be reached without enough failed check-ins
findings.body: When `failure_issue_threshold` is greater than 1, the code slices the most recent check-ins to that threshold length and only bails out when one of them is OK. If the monitor environment has fewer than `failure_issue_threshold` check-ins and none is OK (for example, the first check-in of a new monitor fails), `previous_checkins` can contain a single failure, the OK check is false, and the monitor is marked ERROR with an incident created. This defeats the configured consecutive-failure threshold and produces false incidents for new/sparse monitors. The code should require that the window contains the configured number of check-ins or explicitly count consecutive non-OK statuses before creating the incident.

findings.title: Monitor context returns original config instead of adjusted copy
findings.body: `get_monitor_environment_context()` creates `config = monitor_environment.monitor.config.copy()` and updates `config["schedule_type"]` to the schedule-type display value, but the returned dict uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` rather than `config`. The modified copy is never used, so the `schedule_type` display transformation is discarded and the original mutable config is passed into the occurrence context.
